article.headline: Carvana Jumps 8.8% As Revenue Growth Runs Above 40%
article.deck: Carvana is 7.7% below the 84.01 buy point of a 26-week cup and still 20.4% under its 97.38 high.
body: Carvana runs an online marketplace for buying and selling used cars. It handles the jobs a dealer lot would, from acquiring vehicles and inspecting and reconditioning them to financing, delivery and after-sale support, and it also runs auction sites. The company was founded in 2012 and is based in Tempe, Arizona.

The stock rose 6.28, or 8.8%, to 77.56 on Wednesday, on volume 2.48x its 50-day average. It has gained 21.4% in the past month and 16.7% over 12 months, though it is still down 8.1% this year. Carvana is one of the consumer group's leaders on the desk's list, alongside Airbnb, Ulta and Royal Caribbean, and it ranks 80 of 99 on the desk's RS list.

The growth is in the top line. Revenue rose 42.4% in the September quarter to $8.04 billion, and it climbed in each quarter the table lists: $5.60 billion, $6.43 billion, $7.38 billion, then $8.04 billion. Earnings were 39 cents a share, up 85.7% from a year earlier. Per-share profit has been uneven, though: 84 cents in the December 2025 quarter, then 34 cents, 42 cents and 39 cents.
The market pays for that growth. Carvana is valued at about $85.97 billion and trades at 36.5 times forward earnings and 37.3 times trailing earnings.

The chart is a 26-week cup that corrected 33.4%, from an April 30 high to an Oct. 26 low of 55.92. It formed after a bigger decline: the stock is still below the 97.38 high of Jan. 23 and 20.4% under it. The buy point is 84.01, with the buy range up to 88.21, and the close is 7.7% below it. Wednesday's jump put the stock 17.8% above its 50-day line at 65.85 and 12.5% above the 200-day at 68.94. It is 19.5% above its 21-day exponential line, 2.18 ATRs from the 21-day line, a strong run short of stretched. The RS line is 27.1% below its high, well behind the price recovery.

Carvana reported its quarter Oct. 28. A StockStory headline described the results as operational efficiency and platform expansion driving growth amid margin pressures, and a Stocktwits headline said Carvana was among the leaders of the week's consumer gains. A Trefis headline Wednesday asked whether the stock could crash from here.
The base is not complete. A move through 84.01 would finish it; the RS line still has ground to make up before the chart matches the sales growth.
article.watch: Whether Carvana can carry the move up to the 84.01 buy point, with the 21-day line at 64.91 below.

article.deck: Apple is in the buy range of a 4-week flat base, 1.2% over the 345.44 buy point with room up to 362.71.
body: Apple rose 17.61, or 5.3%, to 349.51 on Wednesday, closing 1.2% above the 345.44 buy point of a 4-week flat base. The base corrected 5.7% from its Sept. 22 high to an Oct. 1 low, and the stock first cleared the buy point on Oct. 22, nine sessions ago, trading 1.17x its 50-day average that day. The buy range runs to 362.71, so the close sits near the bottom of it. Volume Wednesday ran 2.14x the 50-day average.

The close is 1.4% below the 52-week high of 354.47. Apple sits 2.3% above its 21-day exponential line at 341.55 and 4.4% above the 50-day line at 334.84, and the desk flags the move as a rebound off the 50-day. It is 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line: the session's range still reached the line, so the move is nowhere near stretched. Apple ranks 73 of 99 on the desk's RS list, and its RS line is 1.7% below its high. The stock is up 28.6% this year and 29.9% over 12 months.

In the June quarter Apple earned 2.02 a share, up 28.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $109.42 billion, up 16.4%. The table gives no year-over-year comparison for the three quarters before it. The company is valued at about $5.08 trillion and trades at 32.8 times forward earnings.

A Yahoo Finance headline Wednesday said Apple and Microsoft hit all-time highs in the post-election rally, and another argued that post-election gridlock might be a bullish sign for Apple. The stock was at 350.04 after hours, up 0.2%, as of 5:30 p.m. Eastern.
A close back under 345.44 would leave the breakout stalled.
article.watch: Whether Apple holds the 345.44 buy point, with the 21-day line at 341.55 just beneath it.

body: Microsoft rose 34.81, or 6.7%, to 555.80, closing past the 555.55 buy point of a 64-week cup. The base is deep: it ran from a July 31, 2025, high to a June 25 low of 349.20 and corrected 37.1%, more than the one-third O'Neil allows for most cups. The close sits a hair above the buy point, at the very bottom of a buy range that extends to 583.33. Volume ran 2.29x the 50-day average.

The close is 0.6% below the 52-week high of 559.15. Microsoft sits 5.5% above its 21-day exponential line at 526.89 and 7.9% above the 50-day at 515.34. At 1.04 ATRs from the 21-day line, the trend is intact and the move is not stretched. It ranks 72 of 99 on the desk's RS list; the RS line is 5.0% below its high, lagging the price. The stock is up 14.9% this year and 7.5% over 12 months.

In the September quarter Microsoft earned 4.92 a share, up 32.3%, on revenue of $92.28 billion, up 18.8%. Revenue rose in each quarter listed, from $81.27 billion to $82.89 billion to $90.01 billion to $92.28 billion. The next report is due Jan. 27. The company is valued at about $4.13 trillion and trades at 23.0 times forward earnings.

Headlines Wednesday said Apple and Microsoft hit all-time highs in a post-election rally, and that the Dow soared 1,569 points as Microsoft leapt nearly 7%. Another credited the elections and plunging oil for the rally.
With the close this near the buy point, a slip back under 555.55 would leave the breakout stalled.

article.headline: Occidental Petroleum Drops 5.1% As Oil Prices Plunge
article.deck: Occidental's October breakout past 63.87 has stalled: the stock closed 10.2% below the buy point and under its 50-day line.
body: Occidental Petroleum fell 3.10, or 5.1%, to 57.33. The stock broke out on Oct. 23 past the 63.87 buy point of a 6-week flat base, trading 1.39x its 50-day average that day; eight sessions later it closed 10.2% below that buy point, a stalled breakout. The base corrected 14.1% from a Sept. 15 high to a Sept. 29 low of 54.76, and it formed inside a bigger correction: the stock is still under the 67.45 high of March 31. Volume Wednesday ran 1.52x the 50-day average.

Wednesday's drop took Occidental through the 50-day line; it closed 4.7% below the line at 60.15 and 6.4% below the 21-day exponential line at 61.23. It is 1.06 ATRs below the 21-day line, so the whole session traded under it. The stock still sits 1.8% above its 200-day line at 56.32 and 15.0% below its 52-week high. It ranks 66 of 99 on the desk's RS list, and its RS line is 28.6% below its high.

In the June quarter Occidental earned 2.75 a share, up 957.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $8.07 billion, up 53.4%. Results were uneven across the table, including a loss of 7 cents a share in the December 2025 quarter. The next report is due Nov. 9. The company is valued at about $57.31 billion and trades at 11.4 times forward earnings.
A headline Wednesday credited the elections and plunging oil for the broad market rally, a day after another reported oil edged lower as the U.S. bombed Iran before Election Day.
A close back above the 50-day line would repair some of the damage; until then the breakout stays stalled.

article.headline: Merck Climbs 3.9% As The Drugmaker Moves Back Toward Its High
article.deck: Merck is building a 10-week flat base with a 157.02 buy point; the handle high at 151.45 is the early entry.
body: Merck rose 5.69, or 3.9%, to 150.36, 4.2% below the 157.02 buy point of a 10-week flat base. The base ran from an Aug. 25 high to an Oct. 5 low of 138.80 and corrected 11.5%; the buy range would run to 164.87. Wednesday's low touched the 50-day line and the stock closed above it. Volume ran 1.08x the 50-day average.

Two early entries sit just overhead. The handle's Oct. 30 high at 151.45 is 0.7% above the close; clearing it is the aggressive entry ahead of the standard buy point. The 50-day bounce gives an entry at 150.50, above Wednesday's high, with the 50-day line at 146.54 as the stop. The stock sits 2.6% above the 50-day and 3.1% above the 21-day exponential line at 145.88, 0.04 ATRs from the 21-day line. Merck ranks 87 of 99 on the desk's RS list; its RS line is 4.0% off its high. Shares are up 42.8% this year and 82.3% over 12 months, and the close is 4.2% below the 52-week high of 156.92.

The earnings table is mixed. September-quarter earnings came to 2.04 a share, down 12.1%, and the table carries no revenue for that quarter. The two quarters before it were losses, 1.72 a share in March and 54 cents in June, when revenue of $16.61 billion rose 5.1%. The company is valued at about $370.96 billion and trades at 16.7 times forward earnings.
A close above 151.45 would trigger the early entry; a close under the 50-day line would undo the bounce.
article.watch: A move through the 151.45 handle high, with the 50-day line at 146.54 underneath.

aggressive.note: the handle's high from 2026-10-22; clearing it is the early entry, the standard buy point is 120.91

article.headline: Disney Climbs 4.2% As Reports Say Thousands Of Layoffs Are Planned
article.deck: Disney is 1.6% below the 120.91 buy point of a 64-week cup; the early entry at the 113.48 handle high is already well behind it.
body: Walt Disney rose 4.77, or 4.2%, to 118.95, 1.6% below the 120.91 buy point of a 64-week cup. The base ran from a July 29, 2025, high to a March 27 low of 92.19, a 23.7% correction, and the buy range would run to 126.96. The stock has cleared its Oct. 22 handle high of 113.48, the early entry, and now trades 4.8% above it. Volume ran 1.65x the 50-day average.

The close is 0.8% below the 52-week high of 119.96. Disney sits 7.3% above its 21-day exponential line at 110.90 and 10.5% above the 50-day at 107.69, 2.35 ATRs from the 21-day line: a firm run, short of stretched. It ranks 68 of 99 on the desk's RS list, and its RS line is 9.1% below its high, lagging the price. Shares are up 14.3% over the past month and 4.6% this year.

In the June quarter Disney earned 1.51 a share, down 48.3%, on revenue of $25.25 billion, up 6.8%. The next report is due Nov. 17. The company is valued at about $205.39 billion and trades at 15.9 times forward earnings.
Headlines Wednesday said Disney is planning thousands of layoffs in search of 20% cost savings.
A close past 120.91 would complete the base, with the Nov. 17 report close behind.
article.watch: A close above the 120.91 buy point, and the Nov. 17 earnings report.

market_note: The Dow jumped 3.0% to 53,356.12, the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq gained 1.4% to 25,736.51 in Wednesday's post-election rally. The Dow closed 2.3% above its 50-day line, but the S&P 500 finished 0.1% below its own and the Nasdaq 3.0% below. The S&P 500 carries 6 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Nasdaq 5 and the Dow 3, and the desk's state stays Market in correction. Four names on the list broke out Wednesday, Grainger, Microsoft, BlackRock and Fastenal, while software and healthcare carry the highest average RS on the list and the AI infrastructure group lags, with 6% of its members above the 50-day line. After hours, AppLovin jumped 23.1% to 334.56, while CAVA fell 12.4%, HubSpot 8.1%, Qualcomm 7.9% and MercadoLibre 7.6%.

chief.verdict: The post-election rally lifted the Dow 3.0%, the S&P 500 1.6% and the Nasdaq 1.4%, and it produced breakouts in MSFT, BLK, FAST and GWW. But the leadership is old money: industrial distributors, a 64-week deep cup in Microsoft, an asset manager, while AI chips (12% above their 50-day) and AI infrastructure (6%) are still broken. The cleanest bases are short, shallow flat bases in AAPL and MRK, and the best chart, GWW, has already run to the top of its buy range. Risk still leans down: the Nasdaq sits 3.0% under its 50-day and the S&P 0.1% under it, so one up day does not repair this tape.
chief.market: Market in correction with 6 distribution days on the S&P 500 and 5 on the Nasdaq: keep exposure light, take only half-size starter positions in the tightest setups, and add only if the indexes clear and hold their 50-day lines.

picks.why: A tight 4-week flat base only 5.7% deep, and today it bounced off the 50-day line up 5.3% on 2.14 times average volume to close at 349.51, 1.2% past the 345.44 buy point. Earnings came out 2026-11-02, so that event is behind it. The risk is relative strength: RS rank 73, with the RS line 1.7% below its high, is not leader-grade.
picks.entry: Buy between 345.44 and the 362.71 top of the buy range. Clearing the 354.47 52-week high on volume confirms it; a close back under 345.44 means the breakout has failed.

picks.why: RS rank 87, a 10-week flat base 11.5% deep, and today's low touched the 50-day line before a 3.9% close at 150.36, just under the 151.45 handle high from 2026-10-30. Earnings (2026-10-29) are behind it. The risk is the numbers: September-quarter EPS fell 12.1%, and today's volume was only 1.08 times average.
picks.entry: Start a half position above the 151.45 handle high with the 50-day line at 146.54 as the stop; add the rest only on a move through the 157.02 standard buy point.

picks.why: The best chart on the desk: a 15-week flat base 12.9% deep, a breakout up 6.5% on 2.29 times average volume after earnings beat, RS rank 89 and the RS line at a new high. The problem is the price. It closed at 1489.39, 4.9% past the 1420.01 buy point and right at the 1491.01 top of the range, 13.9% above the 50-day and 2.7 ATRs stretched, so the risk is buying the top of a one-day gap.
picks.entry: Wait for a pullback that holds at or above 1420.01 on light volume, or a tight shelf near 1489.39; don't pay above 1491.01.

picks.why: It jumped 6.7% on 2.29 times average volume to 555.80, just 0.0% past the 555.55 buy point, with EPS up 32.3% and sales up 18.8%. But the base is a 64-week deep cup 37.1% deep, the RS line is 5.0% off its high and RS rank is 72, so it is a valid but loose pattern breaking out in a correction.
picks.entry: Buy only if it holds and closes above 555.55 and clears the 559.15 52-week high; the buy range runs to 583.33. A close back below 555.55 kills it.

avoid.why: At 930.67 it is 8.3% past the 859.44 buy point and above the 902.41 top of the range, and it fell 4.4% today on 1.82 times average volume, which is selling, not a fresh entry.
Its breakout came on 0.91 times average volume and has failed: 14.8% under the 51.80 buy point, 9.6% under the 50-day after a 7.3% drop, with earnings on 2026-11-05.
It cut through the 50-day line down 5.1% on 1.52 times average volume, sits 10.2% under the 63.87 buy point with the RS line 28.6% off its high, and reports 2026-11-09, inside five sessions.
The 64-week cup is 23.7% deep, the stock is already 10.5% above its 50-day before reaching the 120.91 buy point, and the last quarter's EPS fell 48.3% with earnings due 2026-11-17.

chief.watch: Whether today's breakouts in MSFT, BLK and FAST hold their buy points of 555.55, 1220.04 and 53.02 tomorrow; if they slip back under, the rally was a one-day event.
